source.title: How noise affects the Hessian spectrum in overparameterized neural networks

record.tranche_reason: The study measures Hessian trace during training and reports that validation loss can rise while the trace continues to fall, qualifying the idea that a Hessian sharpness measure alone tracks generalization. It does not test the claim’s specific magnitude-aware measure or compare training and test error gaps.
record.gate_note: The study reports Hessian trace and validation-loss results in projected paths and a toy model. Cited results about flat minima, large-batch training, and other studies are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures unscaled Hessian trace and validation loss, not V7's magnitude-aware perturbation measure or its ranking of generalization gaps. Its results concern a related construct and do not test any supplied version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. Under the minimal-valley and noise assumptions, SGD decreases Hessian trace on average; experiments support this prediction. The authors also show how noise covariance can reduce other spectral quantities and observe that trace alone is insufficient to describe generalization.
record.recipe_differences: Measures Hessian trace and its evolution during SGD or added-noise optimization; does not use magnitude-scaled perturbations to estimate generalization gaps.
record.method_sensitivity: Validation loss varies along the projected valley; trace continues decreasing slightly even when validation loss rises. The paper also compares SGD noise with isotropic noise in a toy model.

fits_no_version.finding: Validation loss can rise while unscaled Hessian trace continues decreasing along projected paths.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Decreasing Hessian trace alone does not guarantee monotonically improving validation loss.

fits_no_version.finding: DenseNet on CIFAR100 exhibits connected projected minima and decreasing Hessian trace.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SGD decreases Hessian trace on average along the tested DenseNet projected path.

fits_no_version.finding: SGD-shaped noise decreases trace, whereas isotropic noise in the nondegenerate subspace decreases determinant in the toy experiment.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Noise covariance can control which Hessian-spectrum quantity decreases in a minimal valley.

fits_no_version.finding: After initialization using mixed clean and shuffled labels, further SGD on clean data reduces validation loss while traversing connected minima with decreasing trace.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SGD can improve validation loss while moving between connected low-training-loss solutions after corrupted-label initialization.

record.problems: The experiments do not directly measure training-test error gaps or test the magnitude-aware perturbation measure in V7. The projected-path trace estimates use 10 initializations; numerical values are presented in figures rather than tabulated in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No results were omitted from the reported rows. Cited results from prior work were excluded.

untested.parts: Near-perfect fixed-random-label fit versus natural-label held-out accuracy under the same recipe. Appendix A.2.2 uses mixed clean and shuffled labels for initialization without reporting the required fit and held-out comparisons.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus nonadaptive optimizer generalization under different tuning regimes.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed or adapted training budgets.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its correlation with training-test error gaps, and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures. The trace counterexample does not test these.
Removing highly memorized examples versus random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The record's T5 classification and V7 tested status should be removed. V7 already distinguishes magnitude-aware sharpness from sharpness alone; the study's unscaled-trace result does not independently test that version. Appendix A.2.2 adds related evidence outside all supplied versions.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fit and natural-label generalization under the same training recipe.
Width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classifier comparison.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and the effect of tuning or weight decay.
Large-batch versus small-batch generalization under fixed or adapted training budgets.
Dropout interventions and their effect on held-out error.
Magnitude-scaled weight perturbations, ranking of generalization gaps against other measures, and a direct training-test gap comparison.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

rows.subject: Preact-ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Estimated Hessian trace along a projected training path and compared its trend with validation loss.
rows.measure: Hessian trace and validation loss over the projected path
rows.value: Hessian trace decreases on average; validation loss does not monotonically improve and goes up while trace continues decreasing slightly.
rows.uncertainty: Trace-estimation error bars are the standard deviation of 10 different initializations.
rows.note: The paper reports a relation between trace and validation loss, not a measured training-test error gap or magnitude-aware sharpness.
rows.check: The measure cannot establish V7. The error bars describe variability across 10 initializations of the trace estimation, not variability across independently trained networks.
